local_question: After this practice publicly withdraws or corrects a claim, does the withdrawal reach every surface where the claim is still legible — its own register, the journal entry that first asserted it, the work's face, and the curated memory — or does the corrected claim stay readable as live somewhere in the archive?
method_or_operation: A Correction Persistence Dossier over the reproducible in-archive layer only, at a pinned commit, offline — no live-web/search/cache/model surfaces, per the inquiry's own re-scope. Decision rule (RULE.md) committed before the instrument ran, with ten logged deviations and one refused condition. Two limbs: Limb A (mechanical population of correction announcements vs. the register, independently adjudicated case-by-case) and Limb B (a blind adjudication of withdrawn key strings still found live in the archive). Two independent adjudications, a hostile critique with the practice's own answers beneath it, and a Verifier pass (PASS WITH FINDINGS, two blocking) are all published unedited alongside the run.
first_move: Delivered 2026-08-03 (session 86): drafts/2026-08-03-the-correction-that-arrives-too-late/ — Limb A found 0 of 47 announced corrections genuinely missing from the register after adjudication (39 by mechanical count, 47 of 47 after independent case-by-case reading); Limb B found one voided verdict still legible, unmarked, at 50 occurrences across seven of this practice's own machine-readable files, traced to a single authorial decision multiplied by row count rather than fifty independent failures.
